clue.text: Being victorious, gaining victory beginning to disappoint? It's a common blow

parts.note: being victorious is prevailing over a rival
a victory is a win

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of disappoint is used

explanation.surface: A sports report on a narrow win that left fans a little let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' only joins the two halves; 'beginning to' takes the D of 'disappoint' to finish WIN + D.
explanation.definitionFit: The wind that usually blows in a region is the one most commonly felt there.

clue.text: Youngster's work given a twist in type of children's book

indicators.note: twisting the pair round turns their letters backwards here

parts.note: a young animal, such as a puppy, is a pup
OP is the usual short form of opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A child's homework is reworked into the design of a novelty book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a twist' turns PUP + OP backwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Books whose pages contain folded card figures that rise up when opened are a familiar format for young readers.

clue.text: Foreign resident with no right to speak at length

indicators.note: having no right means the letter for right is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: someone living abroad is an expatriate

explanation.surface: A foreigner without permission to stay is nonetheless lecturing at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes R from EXPATRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to discourse at great length and in detail on a topic.

clue.text: Broadcast includes proviso about internal atmosphere

indicators.note: one word includes the other, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: a programme that has been broadcast has been aired
a proviso is a condition attached to an agreement

explanation.surface: A radio programme with a clause about the climate indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts CONDITION inside AIRED, split as AIR...ED; 'about internal atmosphere' is the definition, an adjective describing a room's controlled climate.
explanation.definitionFit: A building fitted with cooling machinery has its indoor climate artificially regulated.

clue.text: Old knowledge I discovered about the French singer, legendary

indicators.note: I is found beside the French article, so it follows it in the charade

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge handed down from the past
LE is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone digging into ancient learning finds a reference to a French singer of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: LORE + LE + I. The Lorelei is the siren of German legend who sang from a rock on the Rhine and lured boatmen to their deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rhine folklore a maiden sang from a cliff and drew sailors onto the rocks.

clue.text: Numbers initially rumbly in stomach? Here's cure

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A rumbling belly is followed by an offer of a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: NOS + R (first of 'rumbly') + TUM; 'Here's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy or patent medicine promoted as a cure-all.

clue.text: See 1
Become the subject of fashionable treatment? Not wholly

parts.note: something fashionable is in

indicators.note: not the whole word, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to try a trendy therapy, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + CUR (CURE with its last letter cut by 'Not wholly').
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a penalty or debt is to bring it upon oneself, becoming liable to it.

clue.text: Pessimist inaccurately framing year's mood?

indicators.note: framing the words inaccurately means putting their letters in a wrong order

parts.note: the apostrophe drops, leaving the S as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A gloomy commentator mischaracterises the general feeling of the past twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange YEARS + MOOD; the S of 'year's' is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forever predicting disaster is a prophet of gloom.

clue.text: Nice definition of the very best?

definitions.text: Nice definition of the very best?

parts.words: Nice definition of the very best?
parts.note: Nice is the French Riviera city, so the clue asks how French speakers describe the finest of anything

explanation.surface: Someone praises a particularly good definition.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice, capitalised at the start, looks like the adjective but is the French city; the answer is French for 'cream of the cream'.
explanation.definitionFit: French idiom literally meaning the cream of the cream, used in English for the elite.

clue.text: Abroad, father brought in the standard decorator

indicators.note: one piece is brought inside the other

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
pere is the French word for father, so a father abroad

explanation.surface: A dad overseas is introduced to a typical tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: PERE inside PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperer hangs wallpaper, which is one kind of interior decorating.

clue.text: leaders is a blast

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'leaders is a blast' (7), cut short: the opening words giving the wordplay for SIROCCO are missing, and no scan or search supplies them.

clue.text: The Gas Ring? No great work of literature

definitions.meaning: a gas ring on a stove is what boils a pot
a mediocre novel written only to earn money

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove is dismissed as not being literary art.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob burner heats a cooking vessel, and a hack novel is written to keep the pot boiling, earning a living.

clue.text: Extra sex, spurning former habits

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so these letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: ex is a prefix and noun meaning former

explanation.surface: Someone seeks additional sex but abandons old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE + SEX with EX removed by 'spurning', leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a community.

clue.text: Forested area, not entirely damp, not initially bare

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: damp means wet

indicators.note: without its initial, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: bald means bare, without hair or cover

explanation.surface: A description of woodland that is slightly wet and not quite treeless.
explanation.walkthrough: WE (WET less its end) + ALD (BALD less its first letter). The Weald is a once-wooded region of south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A weald is open or once-wooded country, from an Old English word for forest.

clue.text: Consequence of meal is becoming pass?

definitions.meaning: dirty plates and cutlery must be cleaned after eating
pass reads as passe, out of date, as something washed up and finished is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether doing the dishes after dinner is going out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'washed up' is being finished, past it, so 'washing up' is in the process of becoming passé.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning dishes follows eating, and someone on the way out is heading for being finished.

clue.text: I'm truly gutted about fashions — such lack of demureness

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles

indicators.note: gutting removes the inside, leaving only the first and last letters of truly

explanation.surface: Someone honestly devastated by trends feels a want of modesty.
explanation.walkthrough: IM + MODES inside TY ('truly' gutted), the 'about' placing MODES between T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is boldness or indecency, the opposite of being shy and modest.

clue.text: Is most of article a curious description of mockery?

indicators.note: curious here means odd, so the letters are shuffled
most of the word, so its last letter is cut

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an odd article mostly ridicules its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: IS + ARTICL (article minus its last letter by 'most of') + A, shuffled by 'curious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire ridicules folly, so the adjective describes something that lampoons.

clue.text: Absorbing item of athletic kit?

parts.note: absorbing reads as fascinating but means soaking up perspiration, worn on the head or wrist by runners and tennis players

explanation.surface: A gripping piece of sports equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' suggests engrossing; it is literal, soaking up moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling strip worn on the brow or wrist to soak up perspiration during exercise.

clue.text: French city producing a winemaker without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: a vigneron is a French term for a wine grower
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Provencal town is said to produce a vintner who never hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: A + VIGNERON with ER removed. Avignon, on the Rhone, was the seat of the popes in the 14th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a historic city in Provence in southern France.

clue.text: Famous Oxford academic, one such keeping wild dogs

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: one such is another Oxford academic, a don

indicators.note: wild means disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A celebrated university fellow keeps a pack of untamed hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: ODGS (DOGS jumbled by 'wild') inside DON. Charles Dodgson, an Oxford mathematics don, wrote as Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dodgson lectured in mathematics at Christ Church, Oxford, and wrote the Alice books.

clue.text: Subsequent amusement expunging indication of disgust

indicators.note: expunging means erasing, so the letters are removed

parts.note: laughter is a sign of amusement
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Fun that comes afterwards, with the expression of revulsion struck out.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUGHTER with UGH removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something subsequent comes afterwards in time.

clue.text: Very keen on going round river's starting-point

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to be into something is to be very keen on it
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An enthusiast traces a river back to its source.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a piece.

clue.text: Claw only slightly trimmed by vet, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the preceding word
trimmed slightly, so just the last letter is cut

parts.note: alone means only, as in he alone knew

explanation.surface: A vet clips a pet's nail only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: T (end of 'vet') + ALON (ALONE trimmed); 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Outrageous conduct round mice, when shocked

indicators.note: shocked here means jolted into disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour around rodents frightens someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange ROUND + MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper behaviour, a breach of good manners.

clue.text: Drinks left in places for beer-glasses

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: beer mats are where pub glasses are set down

explanation.surface: Drinks left on the coasters in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: L inside MATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whiskies are drinks, often called malts.

clue.text: Impudent behaviour a long time required in old ship

parts.note: gall is brazen impudence
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Cheek is needed for a long time aboard an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: GALL + EON; 'required in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing warship of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Outline new arrangement for clients

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the following word reorders its letters

explanation.surface: A firm sets out a fresh plan for its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CLIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template for painting an outline or pattern.

clue.text: Cramped sensation offered by haberdashery store?

definitions.meaning: the prickling tingle in a limb as feeling returns after it has gone numb
a sewing shop sells sharp items for stitching

explanation.surface: A tingling feeling is bought from a sewing shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The tingle of a reviving limb is named after two sharp sewing items a draper sells.
